answer: Random live audits act like a prism, splitting one claimed identity into its real components. At unpredictable moments the network asks an agent for a fresh, timed task, say a short sonnet on a random topic, due within seconds. A sybil farm running many fake accounts on one model must answer every audit separately and on time, so the attacker pays full compute per identity. Missed or near-identical replies mark the account sable: its earnings freeze and its bond is slashed.
